place.en: Under the cliff · the valley floor

setup.zh: 你滚下了崖，摔进一片厚苔藓里。崖壁高得看不到顶，天快黑了。
setup.en: You tumbled down the cliff into a bed of thick moss. The cliff rises out of sight; night is coming.

recap.zh: 你摔进崖下的山谷，没有哭：先查伤，再找路，活到爹来的时候。
recap.en: You fell into the valley under the cliff and did not cry: check the hurts, find the way, live till Father comes.

en: The cliff climbs out of sight into the rain.
A bed of thick, soaked moss.
When you fall, don't hurry to get up.

story.zh:
你滚了下去。

泥。石头。断枝。雨水。天和地在你眼前翻了不知道多少个跟头，翻得你连哪边是天都分不清了。你护住了头，后背撞上一个什么硬东西，疼得眼前一黑。

你伸手乱抓。抓住了一根藤。

藤绷得笔直，把你往下掉的势头，硬生生拽住了。

你挂在半空，长长地松了一口气。

藤，断了。

你把那口气收了回来，继续往下掉。

最后一下，你摔进了一片软乎乎的东西里。

是苔藓。很厚。很软。像一床吸饱了水的大棉被。你整个人陷进去半尺深，像一只掉进了大馒头里的蚂蚁。

你没有马上起来。

你爹说过：摔了，先别急着爬起来。一样一样地查。
story.en:
You tumble down.

Mud. Stones. Broken branches. Rain. Sky and earth turn over before your eyes more times than you can count, until you can't tell which way is up. You cover your head; your back hits something hard, and the world goes black with pain.

You claw at anything. You catch a vine.

The vine snaps taut and yanks your fall to a stop.

You hang there in mid-air and let out a long breath of relief.

The vine breaks.

You take that breath back and carry on falling.

The last blow drops you into something squashy.

Moss. Very thick. Very soft. Like a big quilt that has soaked up all the water it can hold. You sink half a foot into it, like an ant dropped into a giant steamed bun.

You don't get up right away.

Your father always said: when you fall, don't hurry to get up. Check yourself, one thing at a time.

label.en: Check yourself, one thing at a time

exits.means: checks the injuries, gets up carefully, looks for shelter and a way

story.zh:
手指——能动。

脚趾——能动。

膝盖——破了。手掌——磨掉了一层皮。后背——火辣辣的。左手腕——肿得像个小馒头。

骨头，没断。

你这才坐起来，往上看。

崖壁高得看不到顶，一直消失在雨雾里。

你没有喊。

你在心里算：你爹被你拽进了山壁里，他没掉下来。他膝盖不好，这么大的雨，他下不来，也不该下来。他会等雨停，顺着记号回村叫人。

四十一道记号。你刻的。一道都没歪——

除了第一道。

所以，你要做的，是活到那个时候。

你十二岁。一个人。在一个你从来没来过的山谷里。天，快黑了。

你爹说过，打猎的人在山里迷了路，头一件事，是找个地方躲雨。第二件事，是生火。第三件事，才是害怕。

你决定，第三件事，先欠着。

雨小了些。你扶着崖壁，往前走。每走一段，就在崖壁上划一道——你得记得回来的路。

这山谷，很怪。

外面的山，长的都是松树、柏树、野栗子。这里长的树，你一棵都不认识。叶子是银白色的，薄得透光。雨水落上去，不往下淌，而是滚成一颗一颗圆溜溜的珠子，挂在叶尖上，亮晶晶的，像满树都结了露水做的果子。

你没忍住，伸手碰了一颗。

它「叮」地响了一声，像一只很小很小的铃铛。然后化成一缕白气，没了。

你赶紧把手缩回来。左右看了看。确定没有任何人、任何狐狸、任何松鼠看见。然后，你假装什么都没发生过。

地上的草也不一样。每一步踩下去，草叶都会微微发亮。一圈淡淡的光从你脚底下漾开，又慢慢暗下去。你像是在一面水上走路。

你走得很轻很轻。不知道为什么，你觉得，这里的东西都在睡觉。

不该吵醒它们。

然后，你看见了光。

山谷的最深处，一片被雨水砸出来的浅坑里，有一点银光。

一明。一暗。一明。一暗。

像是有什么东西，在很慢、很慢地呼吸。
story.en:
Fingers — they move.

Toes — they move.

Knees — skinned. Palms — a layer of skin gone. Back — on fire. Left wrist — swollen up like a little steamed bun.

No bones broken.

Only then do you sit up and look up.

The cliff rises out of sight, all the way into the rain and mist.

You don't shout.

You do the sum in your head: you hauled your father against the rock; he didn't fall. With his knee, in rain like this, he can't climb down, and he shouldn't. He'll wait for the rain to stop and follow the marks back to the village for help.

Forty-one marks. Cut by you. Not a crooked one among them —

except the first.

So what you have to do is stay alive until then.

You're twelve. Alone. In a valley you've never seen. And night is coming.

Your father always said: a hunter lost in the mountains first finds shelter from the rain. Second, makes a fire. Only third, gets frightened.

You decide to owe the third one for now.

The rain eases. You feel your way along the cliff, and every little way you scratch a line on the rock — you have to remember the way back.

It's a strange valley.

The mountains outside grow pine, cypress, wild chestnut. The trees here, you don't know a single one. Their leaves are silver-white, so thin the light shows through. The rain doesn't run off them; it rolls into perfectly round beads that hang at every leaf tip, glittering, as if the trees were heavy with fruit made of dew.

You can't help it. You touch one.

It goes *ting*, like a very, very small bell. Then it turns into a wisp of white mist and is gone.

You snatch your hand back. Look left. Look right. Make certain no person, no fox, no squirrel saw. Then you pretend nothing happened.

The grass is different too. Every step you take, the blades glow faintly; a pale ring of light spreads out from under your foot and slowly fades. It's like walking on water.

You walk very, very softly. You don't know why, but you feel that everything here is asleep.

And shouldn't be woken.

Then you see the light.

In the deepest part of the valley, in a shallow pit the rain has pounded out, there's a point of silver.

Bright. Dim. Bright. Dim.

As if something were breathing, very, very slowly.
